text:
Maria: heads up — CI turned red on master during the nightly run. flaky unit: serve.TestRetryOrdering failing intermittently (only on CI, passes locally most of the time).
CI Bot: job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/infra/1485 — failed test: serve.TestRetryOrdering — logs attached. exit code 1, got timeout on step 'retry scheduler'.
Liam: saw this one before, usually nondeterministic ordering between the backoff timer and in-flight cancel. Sometimes repros with -race, sometimes not.
Jay: can you paste the snippet of the failing assertion from the log?
Maria: from the CI log: ```--- FAIL: TestRetryOrdering (0.32s)
    retry_test.go:128: expected 2 retries, got 1
    retry_test.go:142: observed ordering: [send, cancel, retry]```
Sarah: hmm. Is anyone running the test with a deterministic seed? We have test helpers that respect REDWOOD_TEST_SEED.
Liam: not for this one, but I can try `REDWOOD_TEST_SEED=0 go test ./serve -run TestRetryOrdering -count=100`. that often surfaces a pattern.
Maria: trying a 50-run locally now. results so far: 0/50 fail. CI is reproducible ~1 in 20.
Jay: let's queue a seed-sweep on CI rather than manual. DevOps Bot: I've queued job https://ci.redwood.ai/job/seed-sweep/serve-2219876500 with 200 runs (seeds 1..200) under a dedicated worker pool.
CI Bot: seed-sweep job started, will post summary when done.
Liam: also try `GOMAXPROCS=1` — a lot of these ordering races collapse to single-thread and then repros either vanish or become deterministic.
Sarah: if GOMAXPROCS alters it, that points to a scheduling race. Could add a short mutex in test to serialize event ordering as an experiment.
Maria: plan: 1) let the seed-sweep run, 2) try GOMAXPROCS=1 sweep, 3) if repro, bisect commit range (last_green..head) to narrow change that increased flake rate.
Jay: I can take the bisect if seed-sweep returns a stable failing seed. ping me with the failing seed+CI job link.
DevOps Bot: FYI I added an ephemeral job `serve-flake-debug` that will run the failing test in a loop with verbose logs and timestamps. Command: `REDWOOD_TEST_SEED=$SEED GOMAXPROCS=$GOMAXPROCS go test -run TestRetryOrdering -v -count=1`.
Maria: thx. also tagging the PR that landed a retry refactor yesterday — @Jay @Liam please sanity-check the change for any relaxed ordering assumptions.
Liam: will review later today. if we can reproduce deterministically I'll open a temporary skip or mark unstable so master stays green.
Sarah: if we skip, add a follow-up ticket linking to the seed/bisect output. we should avoid long-term flakes.
Maria: agreed. will update this thread when seed-sweep finishes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
CI Bot: seed-sweep finished: 200 runs, 11 failures. failing seeds: [7, 23, 56, 89, 101, 117, 148, 162, 173, 189, 194]. most failures show the same "expected 2 retries, got 1" pattern.
Maria: perfect — Jay, Liam, I'll DM the first failing seed and the `serve-flake-debug` logs. next step is bisect on last_green..HEAD unless someone objects.
Jay: go for bisect. I'll run a binary search across commits and report back.
Sarah: thanks everyone. quick note for postmortem: include guidance to use REDWOOD_TEST_SEED in new timing-sensitive tests and add a small harness utility for ordered event simulation to reduce flakiness.
Maria: closing the loop — created ticket RD-4248 to track the fix + flaky test cleanup, assigning to @Liam.
